2607.21051.title: Sample-Efficient Learning from Agent Experience
2607.21051.paper_summary: Real-world agent learning is often constrained by costly environment interactions, such as running time-consuming experiments or obtaining human feedback. In-context learning offers a highly sample-efficient way for agents to learn from their own interaction histories, but its gains disappear once that experience is removed from the context. Separately, context distillation provides a mechanism for internalizing contextual information into model weights. However, applying it to agents' interaction histories without sacrificing environment sample efficiency remains underexplored. We term this problem Experience Distillation and develop an implementation that requires no further environment interaction beyond the collected experience. Experiments on 749 curated software-engineering tasks and six text-adventure games show that it retains at least 64.8\% of the gains from in-context learning across both domains, whereas direct supervised fine-tuning on the collected experience recovers only 3.8\%. Compared with classical reinforcement-learning baselines, in-context learning from trial-and-error experience followed by Experience Distillation matches their performance with at least \(9.6\times\) fewer environment samples.
2607.21051.paper_summary_zh: 現實世界中的代理學習常常受到昂貴的環境互動的限制，例如進行耗時的實驗或獲取人類反饋。上下文學習為代理從自身互動歷史中學習提供了一種高效的樣本利用方式，但一旦該經驗從上下文中移除，其收益便會消失。另一方面，上下文蒸餾提供了一種將上下文信息內化為模型權重的機制。然而，將其應用於代理的互動歷史而不犧牲環境樣本效率仍然未被充分探索。我們將這個問題稱為經驗蒸餾，並開發了一種實現方式，該方式不需要進一步的環境互動，只需收集到的經驗。對749個精心策劃的軟體工程任務和六個文本冒險遊戲的實驗表明，它在這兩個領域中保留了至少64.8\%的上下文學習收益，而對收集到的經驗進行直接監督微調僅恢復了3.8\%。與經典的強化學習基準相比，從試錯經驗中進行的上下文學習隨後經過經驗蒸餾，其性能匹配了基準，且環境樣本數量至少減少了\(9.6\times\)。
